Name: Hector Quintanilla
Question: How do I take advantage of a dropping stock?
Answer: In 2000, Amazon shares fell 80%. Here’s how Jeff Bezos responded: Here’s the text for better reading: To our shareholders: Ouch. It's been a brutal year for many in the capital markets and certainly for Amazon shareholders. As of this writing, our shares are down more than 80% from when I wrote you last year. Nevertheless, by almost any measure, Amazon the company is in a stronger position now than at any time in its past. - We served 20 million customers in 2000, up from 14 million in 1999. - Sales grew to $2.76 billion in 2000 from $1.64 billion in 1999. - Pro forma operating loss shrank to 6% of sales in Q4 2000, from 26% of sales in Q4 1999. - Pro forma operating loss in the U.S. shrank to 2% of sales in Q4 2000, from 24% of sales in Q4 1999. - Average spend per customer in 2000 was $134, up 19%. - Gross profit grew to $656 million in 2000, from $291 million in 1999, up 125%. - Almost 36% of Q4 2000 U.S. customers purchased from one of our “non-BMV” stores such as electronics, tools, and kitchen. - International sales grew to $381 million in 2000, from $168 million in 1999. - We helped our partner Toysrus sell more than $125 million of toys and video games in Q4 2000. - We ended 2000 with cash and marketable securities of $1.1 billion, up from $706 million at the end of 1999, thanks to our early 2000 euroconvert financing. - And, most importantly, our heads-down focus on the customer was reflected in a score of 84 on the American Customer Satisfaction Index. We are told this is the highest score ever recorded for a service company in any industry. So, if the company is better positioned today than it was a year ago, why is the stock price so much lower than it was a year ago? As the famed investor Benjamin Graham said, “In the short term, the stock market is a voting machine; in the long term, it's a weighing machine.” Clearly there was a lot of voting going on in the boom year of '99—and much less weighing. We're a company that wants to be weighed, and over time, we will be—over the long term, all companies are. In the meantime, we have our heads down working to build a heavier and heavier company. To answer your question, how do I take advantage of a falling stock? In Bezos words: “In the short term, the stock market is a voting machine; in the long term, it’s a weighing machine.” Bezos emphasizes that while stock prices can be volatile and influenced by short-term sentiment, the true value of a company is revealed over time through its fundamentals. As investors, we should focus on the long-term potential and underlying health of a business rather than getting emotionally distracted by short-term market movements. #BeBusinessSmart

Name: Hector Quintanilla
Question: Why do humans say ‘I have no time’?
Answer: I was living one of the most stressful seasons of my life when I learned this lesson… My days were filled nonstop. I had three weeks to deliver a new student housing building to my local university. They already had dozens of students with pre-signed leases ready to get in. On top of this, I was studying my part-time MBA, while also managing my family life. Amid this “storm,” one day time stopped. My 10-month-old daughter woke up one night screaming with abdominal pain. She was clearly suffering. Scared, we rushed her to the ER, where doctors couldn’t understand what was happening. Desperation took over. After what felt like hours, they finally diagnosed her with intussusception, a rare disorder that affects some infants. Thankfully, doctors took immediate action and solved the problem. We stayed at the hospital for three days. During that time, I couldn't work. It was during these days that I learned a huge lesson: We don’t have time; we MAKE the time to make things happen. We don’t TRY to find the time — we do whatever it takes to make it happen. I learned that my “lack of time” is very frequently hiding my lack of commitment. The truth is that if it’s important, I ALWAYS find a way. If it’s not important, I find an excuse. When I commit to my goals, I MAKE THE TIME. To me, time management is all about priorities. What do you think? Do we find time, or do we make the time to accomplish things? #BeBusinessSmart

Name: Hector Quintanilla
Question: How do you know when to give up on a startup idea?
Answer: When is the Right Time to Quit a FAILING Business? Very difficult situation: “Should I keep pushing or is it time to step back?” A tough question I’ve faced several times… This is what I would consider if I would be facing this today: 1. Am I in a growing industry? If I’m working in a market that’s expanding, it might be worth keeping up the hustle. Growth means opportunity. If my industry is booming, I wouldn’t quit just yet. 2. Is execution the problem? Tough truth: Two teams, same product, same ideas, same market, same money —yet different results. Why? Execution. Great execution is the result of amazing people. If my execution sucks, I’ll try to fix this first. 3. Do I have the right product? Sometimes it’s important to analyze my competitors and be brutally honest —do I stand a chance against them? If not, I might be needing to face a different reality….Shut down! 4. Do I have the right systems and processes? Ask, am I going crazy? Efficiency matters. Could I possibly change this? Fixing my process before throwing in the towel could be critical to consider. 5. Are my customers happy? In today’s marketplace, good isn’t good enough. I need my customers to be excited, amazed and thrilled about my product or service. If I’ve got a shot at delivering that, I’ll keep pushing. If not, I wouldn’t waste more time. 6. Could my pride or fear of facing the reality be getting in the Way? I hate failure as much as anyone else, but sometimes I’ve just got to be humble. The entrepreneurial journey is all about trial and error. Sometimes, I need to take my losses, learn, and move on. Here’s the brutal truth: deep down, I believe we already know the answer but we can be hoping for a miracle to avoid the painful truth. Recognizing it’s time to move on can take weeks, months, or even years. The longer I wait, the more damage I do to myself and my wallet. The time I waste today is time I’m losing to push forward the right venture. Fail fast and move on… this is a key entrepreneurial skill we must develop ASAP. Remember, your energy is worth much more than a bad business. #BeBusinessSmart

Question: Why should you be selling the solution and not your products?
Answer: "Can you help me?" my wife asked me as soon as I got home. “What’s wrong?” "None of the laundry's power outlets are working." "Sure, let me check it out," I confidently said. My wife knows I have zero handyman skills, but I was willing to push my luck. "What could be wrong?" I wondered. "The lights are working fine. Maybe the device you're trying to plug in isn't working." I quickly grabbed my wife's hairdryer and plugged it in. "Nothing," I said. "Maybe it’s a tripped breaker," I told her while walking out to check the main breaker box. “Got it?” she asked anxiously. “Nothing! Everything seems to be working fine," I replied. "I don't know what's wrong. Call the electrician." I said. A few hours later, the electrician arrived. As soon as I showed him the problem, he immediately walked out to the garage, found a GFCI outlet on the back wall of our laundry, clicked the RESET button, and said, "Done. You can test it now." "It works!" my wife said with a big smile. Meanwhile, I stood there feeling like a fool. It took this guy literally TWO MINUTES to solve the problem! "How much do I owe you?" I asked. "$100," he said. "What? One hundred dollars for clicking the reset button?" I exclaimed. "Sir," he respectfully answered, "I charged you $1 for clicking the RESET button and $99 for making the trip to find the solution for you." OUCH... Remember, DO NOT sell your time; sell the solution! #BeBusinessSmart

Answer: Captain “Sully” had only 208 seconds to land the Airbus in the Hudson River… Here the 208 seconds from the black box recording: 3:27 pm The plane is at an altitude of 3,000 feet directly above The Bronx and traveling at 250mph when it encounters a flock of Canada geese. The birds are sucked into both of the plane’s engines which fail immediately. 3:27 pm Air traffic controller, contacts Flight 1549, whose call-sign is “Cactus”, to request a routine course-correction. Sullenberger, who has spent the previous seconds trying to restart the engines, responds: “Ah, this is, uh, Cactus 1549, hit birds. We lost thrust in both engines. We’re turning back towards LaGuardia.” 3:28 pm With no thrust and little altitude, he knows that a turn back to LaGuardia is not viable. “I am not sure if we can make any runway,” he tells controller. “What’s over to our right? Anything in New Jersey? Maybe Teterboro?” A few seconds later the controller comes with the confirmation. “Cactus 1549, turn right two eight zero. You can land Runway 1 at Teterboro.” By now Sully had decided that this too was not viable. “We can’t do it.” Controller: “O.K. Which runway would you like at Teterboro?” Sullenberger: “We’re gonna be in the Hudson.” Controller: “I’m sorry, say again, Cactus?” 3:28 pm Sully begins his glide towards the Hudson. The only major obstacle in his way is the Washington Bridge, which he clears with about 900 feet to spare. 3:30 pm Sully makes his only announcement to the passengers. “Brace for impact.” Inside the cabin, the flight attendants repeat the instruction. “Brace! Brace! Heads down! Stay down!” 3:31 pm With its nose raised and traveling at 150mph US Airways Flight 1549 completes an unpowered ditching in the Hudson. All 155 passengers and crew on board US Airways Flight 1549 survived. This extraordinary landing makes me wonder, what are the odds of a rookie pilot accomplishing this? To me, the idea that “educated” people are those trained with technical skills is now outdated. Why? Because technical skills are focused on HOW to do the job, NOT on WHAT jobs to do. To make wise decisions, not necessarily to execute the surgery. How do real estate investors make money? By knowing which property to buy, not by merely buying a property. It’s time to STOP obsessing over improving our technical skills — technology will do that! Strive to become an expert in the context of WHERE your skills are used. The value (the money) is now found in your ability to make wise, strategic decisions, NOT on doing what thousands of people or machines can do. In brief, stop chasing degrees — pursue domain expertise. What do you think? Share👇 #BeBusinessSmart

Name: Hector Quintanilla
Question: How does a profitable company go bankrupt?
Answer: If we're profitable, why worry, right? Well, for me, last week reality struck... Last week I shared with my newsletter subscribers how I'm growing a newly launched polyurethane adhesives business from $0 to $500K with zero overhead. Over the past few months, I've been focused solely on the profits shown in my P&L statements. But despite these profits, I'm struggling to grow my orders and pay my suppliers due to low cash reserves. That's when my accountant highlighted the crucial difference between profit and cash flow. To my surprise, most of my revenue is stuck in accounts receivable, making it difficult to cover expenses and support growth initiatives that require immediate cash. As entrepreneurs, most of us instinctively aim to buy cheap and sell for a profit. We want more sales and pursue growth... As you can see, I hate accounting and I'm bad at it! Unlike my other ventures, this business demands that I keep an eye on both the P&L and cash flow statements. A new lesson learned: A healthy P&L doesn't always mean a healthy business! To turn things around, we're tightening our credit terms, pursuing overdue payments more aggressively, and adjusting our spending to align with actual cash availability. So, to answer your question, how does a profitable company go bankrupt? Cash flow is like the oxygen that sustains a business alive! #BeBusinessSmart

I jealously protect my freedom. But freedom without accountability is dangerous! Enjoying freedom without accountability opens the door for me to procrastinate, avoid difficult tasks, and make excuses. Whenever I find myself in a perpetual loop of planning without executing, I know I'm lacking accountability! A common excuse is, "I like working at my own pace." Accountability isn't just about meeting deadlines; it's about taking ownership of my goals, being humble about my struggles, learning from mistakes, and pushing through the uncomfortable tasks that need to be done. So, to answer your question, what are the challenges solopreneurs face? Most solopreneurs struggle to make progress. Ask yourself: Are you truly holding yourself accountable? Question: What are some common mistakes people make when they have a side hustle?

Here is what many side hustlers do: 1. Run ads 2. Get traffic 3. Get leads 4. Make a sale 5. Profit This can work momentarily, but it's not a scalable and predictable business model in the long run. This is why most struggle and never feel secure enough to ever quit. If you want to make the leap to your full-time business, you need a predictable system to bring in the sales. Because this is for certain, costs always rise and competitors get tougher over time, meaning each year, margins get chomped away. The solution… Build a customer acquisition system for your business, and focus on increasing your customer lifetime value, not just reducing acquisition costs. Here's what that looks like: 1. Run ads 2. Get traffic 3. Get leads 4. Acquire a customer 5. Deliver results to them 6. Sell them other (high ticket) products or services 7. Profit 8. Invest profits into more growth. Focus on MRR and you will have a chance to win the market. Stop chasing, start building. There's no other way. #BeBusinessSmart

Question: Why do I feel anxious about executing my goals?
Answer: I always remember what my dad used to tell me whenever I was getting too anxious trying to accomplish big goals. He’d say, “Hector, remember that slow and steady wins the race. People who do well don’t rush or take huge risks. Good things need time, so be patient!” “But how can I control the frustration of feeling I’m not making any progress?” I asked. “You’re focused on the outcome, not on the process.” He said. I was still confused. “Please explain,” I said. “Rather than concentrating on outcome-based goals, shift your focus to process-based goals. These are the things you can control and achieve. This perspective has worked for me, try it.” “Can you give me an example, dad?” “Sure, for example, consider setting these outcome-based goals like, ‘winning a race’ or ‘increasing your business profits by 20%.’ To achieve these goals, it will depend on many factors, some of which most likely be out of your control. On the other hand, ‘training every day for an hour’ or ‘improving customer service in your business.’ These are within your control because they’re about what you can do. Focusing on process-based goals can lead to a more satisfying outcomes because you can feel that sense of accomplishment as you complete them.” That helped me a lot. Question: What are the most inspiring short stories?
Answer: From Stocking Shelves at a Grocery Store to Becoming a Super Bowl MVP champion. The Inspiring story of Kurt Warner… Warner is the only undrafted player to win an NFL MVP award and a Super Bowl MVP award. Early in his career, he went undrafted in the 1994 NFL Draft after playing college football at the University of Northern Iowa. Warner was later invited to try out for the Green Bay Packers but was cut from the team even before the season began. To make ends meet, Warner took a job stocking shelves at a grocery store in Cedar Falls, Iowa, for $5.50 an hour. But he never gave up on his dream. Driven by his passion and determination, he continued to train and stay in shape. Warner eventually made his way into the Arena Football League, where he showcased his skills, proving he could play quarterback in the NFL. Four long years after going undrafted in 1994, Warner signed with the St. Louis Rams as a backup quarterback in 1998. The following year, an injury to the starting quarterback gave Warner his first chance to lead the team. Seizing the opportunity, Warner delivered an MVP season that year, throwing for over 4,300 yards and 41 touchdowns, leading the Rams to a victory in Super Bowl XXXIV. Warner's performance that season is one of the most remarkable single-season performances in NFL history, and the only undrafted player to win an NFL MVP award and a Super Bowl MVP award. After two other Super Bowl attempts, Warner retired in 2010 and was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2017. Never underestimate the power of passion and perseverance! #BeBusinessSmart

Question: What advice would you like to offer for the new year?
Answer: Sir Anthony Hopkins extraordinary wisdom: Let go the people who are not prepared to love you. Stop showing up for people who have no interest in your presence. I know your instinct is to do everything to earn the appreciation of those around you, but it's a boost that steals your time, energy, mental and physical health. When you begin to fight for a life with joy, interest and commitment, not everyone will be ready to follow you in this place. This doesn't mean you need to change what you are, it means you should let go of the people who aren't ready to accompany you. If you are excluded, insulted, forgotten or ignored by the people you give your time to, you don't do yourself a favor by continuing to offer your energy and your life. The truth is that you are not for everyone and not everyone is for you. That's what makes it so special when you meet people who reciprocate love. You will know how precious you are. The more time you spend trying to make yourself loved by someone who is unable to, the more time you waste depriving yourself of the possibility of this connection to someone else. There are billions of people on this planet and many of them will meet with you at your level of interest and commitment. The more you stay involved with people who use you as a pillow, a background option or a therapist for emotional healing, the longer you stay away from the community you want. Maybe if you stop showing up, you won't be wanted. Maybe if you stop trying, the relationship will end. Maybe if you stop texting your phone will stay dark for weeks. That doesn't mean you ruined the relationship, it means the only thing holding it back was the energy that only you gave to keep it. This is not love, it's attachment. It's wanting to give a chance to those who don't deserve it. You deserve so much, there are people who should not be in your life. The most valuable thing you have in your life is your time and energy, and both are limited. When you give your time and energy, it will define your existence. When you realize this, you begin to understand why you are so anxious when you spend time with people, in activities, places or situations that don't suit you and shouldn't be around you, your energy is stolen. You will begin to realize that the most important thing you can do for yourself and for everyone around you is to protect your energy more fiercely than anything else. Make your life a safe haven, in which only ′′compatible′′ people are allowed. You are not responsible for saving anyone. You are not responsible for convincing them to improve. It's not your work to exist for people and give your life to them! If you feel bad, if you feel compelled, you will be the root of all your problems, fearing that they will not return the favors you have granted. It's your only obligation to realize that you are the love of your destiny and accept the love you deserve. Decide that you deserve true friendship, commitment, true and complete love with healthy and prosperous people. Then wait and see how much everything begins to change. Don't waste time with people who are not worth it. Change will give you the love, the esteem, happiness and the protection you deserve.” Happy New Year! #BeBusinessSmart

The damage was estimated to be around $7 million dollars at the time, which is equivalent to over $180 million today. Insurance only covered $2.3 million. How would you react if your entire life's work went up in flames at 67 years of age? Thank God we can start anew.” Edison wasted no time in rebuilding. In just a few weeks after the fire, parts of the lab were operational again. Within about a year, most of the facilities were fully reconstructed. To answer your question, what is the best way to deal with failure at everything in life? Question: Why is knowing your customer important?
Answer: Here’s the story behind the Mustang Phenomenon… On April 17, 1964, the Ford Mustang was unveiled. While many at Ford hadn't expected the Mustang to be a success, Lee Iacocca stood strong with a clear vision for the car. Lee wasn't building another car; he was focused on giving America a new way to drive. At the time, most cars were seen as transportation tools. Meanwhile, he envisioned a car that was about the joy of driving. The Mustang became an instant phenomenon, influencing a whole generation. Ford initially hoped to sell 100,000 units in the first year. Astonishingly, they surpassed that by selling one million cars in just 18 months! Lee Iacocca's vision for the Mustang reminds me of the importance of being customer-centric and avoiding the dangers of being too product-centric. Iacocca didn't assume he knew what people wanted. He listened to consumers and delivered on their desires. The Mustang revolutionized transportation, giving the driver a sense of freedom, lifestyle, and personal expression. A solid reminder that we don't buy products — we buy experiences, emotions, and solutions to problems. To answer your question, why is knowing your customer important? The Mustang story is a perfect example of the profound impact of understanding your customer's deepest desires. Start with the customer in mind. That's the first step towards crafting your own 'Mustang moment.' #BeBusinessSmart

Question: What are the most common mistakes made by small to medium business owners?
Answer: Meet Don Jose, a restaurant host who was worth more than a Michelin Star... For over two decades, Don Jose was the face of a popular restaurant in my hometown. He had a unique gift for remembering names and even your favorite dish. As soon as you walked in, Don Jose greeted everyone, making you feel like the most important person in the world. Believe me, the food was good, but it was Don Jose's attention to detail that made this restaurant unforgettable. Then, the unexpected happened. For some unexplained reason, Don Jose switched to another restaurant. Here's where it gets interesting: people followed Don Jose, and the old restaurant eventually closed its doors. Meanwhile, the new place? Thriving! I've always been amazed by why hundreds of customers followed Don Jose to a completely different establishment. Was it the food? Nope, he wasn't the cook. Location? Not really; the old restaurant was actually in a better location. Clearly, their success was based on selling the experience that Don Jose gave to every customer who walked in. When Don Jose moved, he didn't just carry his exceptional hosting skills with him; he carried the heart and soul of a community he'd built over 20 years. Now, to answer your question, what are the most common mistakes made by small to medium business owners? This is important. In business, put people first, and success will follow. Whether you're selling tacos or software — it's the people who make the business. Are you and your team giving customers a good reason to keep coming back? Once you've got that down, you're not just serving customers; you're building a reputation. And that is the key recipe for long-term success. #BeBusinessSmart

Name: Hector Quintanilla
Question: Why do rich people work even after they become rich? Why don't they play?
Answer: "Dad, when will you retire?" I asked him one day. "Hector, I retired before you were born," he laughed. Confused, I asked again, "Be honest, Dad, I mean, when will you stop working?" His response was simple, "Working? What's work? I don't know what work is." “OK, Dad, forget about it,” I said as I assumed he wasn't willing to talk about this. "Hector,” he said, “what you know as my job is not work for me. I enjoy architecture so much that I could do this 24/7. This is who I am. Architecture is my life.” So, to answer your question, why do rich people work even after they become rich? Why don't they play? My father lived to be 91 and worked until his body gave up on him. He was a passionate architect who found joy in his work. That's what kept him active and full of joy every day. His passion for architecture was infectious, and it taught me this valuable lesson about work as a lifestyle. So, if you ask me about retirement or work-life balance, I'd say it's better to find what you love and make it a part of your life. When you find that, you’ll stop working and start living. We achieve a balance not by separating work from life but by integrating what you love into your lifestyle. Today, this is how I see it: It's not about working less; it's about loving more what you do. That's the secret to a fulfilling life. As my father always said, "The day you find what you love is when you will stop working." So, go out there and find your passion. Make it your lifestyle. And remember, it's not work when you love what you do. #BeBusinessSmart

Answer: I have a friend who literally goes crazy when his favorite team scores or wins. Question: What are some crisis management techniques?
Answer: In the early 1970s, the Ford Motor Company was facing two massive problems: As a result the automaker found itself with a surplus of unsold Mavericks sitting on their dealer lots. Parking the unsold Mavericks above ground would have damaged the new cars and cause other long-term problems. Ford decided to store the unsold Mavericks in the Subtropolis caves located in Kansas City, Missouri. The caves proved to be the ideal climate-controlled environment for several months until the market improved. At its peak, Ford stored as many as 14,000 Mavericks in the caves. The cars were organized in neat rows, and employees were responsible to move them occasionally to prevent any damage from them sitting in one place for too long. Question: What are the best ways to improve your body language?
Answer: I’ll never forget the first time I spoke in public; I was super nervous! Luckily I had my wife with me at that event, so a few hours before my presentation, she encouraged me to practice. A minute after I started, she started waving her hands at me, saying, “Stop... stop... stop!” I tried to ignore her, focusing on my presentation. “Hector, I said stop! You’ve got to hold a tall and straight posture,” she said. “Got it,” I replied, lifting myself. I started my presentation again. “Stop... stop... stop!” she urged again a few minutes later. “Now, what’s wrong,” I asked. “You can’t achieve eye contact if your face is gazing toward the ground. Keep your neck and head held high.” “Okaaaaaay,” I replied, frustrated, now holding my head straight up and towards the audience. I started my presentation for a third time... again, she stopped me! “Now, what?” I questioned, starting to get irritated at her interruptions. “Honey, you’re dragging your feet!” “Ohh wow,” I thought while correcting my lousy body language. “Hector, I need to see you are showing yourself confident and proud of your presentation,” she urged. “Do you have any idea how stressful this is?” I asked. “I know this is stressful, but you can do it! Now, remember to keep your movements natural. Hold your chin up, and your arms should rest comfortably alongside your hips. Remember never to cross your arms.” “Got it!” I said. As I finally finished the presentation, she immediately ran towards me to hug me and said, “Now you’re ready. You will do great. I’m proud of you!” I’m so thankful I had my wife’s feedback that morning. Her feedback helped me feel more confident when I jumped on the stage. Success! Now, to answer your question, what are the best ways to improve your body language? If you don’t present yourself as an authoritative and trustworthy person, you’ll never get the respect you need to succeed on stage and in life. Some of the best ways to improve your body language include paying attention to your posture, making eye contact, using gestures, and being aware of your tone. Question: What are the biggest marketing mistakes made by startups?
Answer: In 1886, a pharmacist named John Pemberton created a carbonated beverage, which he initially sold as a medicinal drink. He named the drink Coca-Cola. The name "Coca-Cola" originated from two ingredients used in the drink, coca leaves, and kola nuts. Coca leaves were traditionally used for their stimulant properties. The kola nut was a natural source of caffeine. The name Coca-Cola resulted from combining the two main ingredients (Coca & Kola) and intentionally placing the two "C's" in the beverage's name. The early market for the Coca-Cola drink focused on its presumed medicinal properties, using slogans like "Delicious and Refreshing" and "The Ideal Brain Tonic." However, following this strategy, Pemberton struggled to keep the business afloat. One year later, Pemberton's bookkeeper, Mr. Frank Mason Robinson, presented the founder with the Coca-Cola name in cursive letters. This became the company's logo. Robinson also came up with the famous slogan "The Pause That Refreshes." which was first used in advertising in 1901. This new catchphrase communicated the product's benefit in a simple and memorable way, suggesting that Coca-Cola was not just a drink but a refreshing break from the everyday routine or a moment of relaxation and enjoyment. This slogan helped Coca-Cola differentiate and position itself as a refreshing and desirable drink. With this new logo and slogan, the sales of Coca-Cola began to take off. In 1888, the Coca-Cola secret recipe and rights to the brand were eventually sold to Asa Griggs Candler for $2,300, who expanded the market by bottling the drink and selling it across the country. Coca-Cola's marketing strategies have continued to evolve over the years, using celebrity endorsements, catchy jingles, and memorable advertising campaigns to maintain its top brand. Now to answer your question, what are the biggest marketing mistakes made by startups? I’ve seen too many small businesses fail because of their inability to communicate their product or service effectively to their target market. “A good business strategy is worth more than a lifetime of hard work.” — Hector Quintanilla. Answer: It’s not easy to see your father cry… I remember how depressed and emotionally drained I found myself after the 2008 financial meltdown. To make some income, your grandfather had to work in the middle of the desert building roads that the government invested to keep people busy.” My father started to accumulate tears in his eyes as he remembered, “Your grandfather would leave our home for weeks. His working conditions where under extreme heat. Venomous snakes everywhere. We had no communication. Uncertainty and fear filled our family.” He paused as he collected his memories. “Your grandma struggled. There was no sunscreen back then. I can’t describe how physically damaged his body was every time he returned.” I sat there speechless. “Now THAT is tough Hector,” he said staring at me. “Yet I never saw your grandfather complain even once!” My dad then grabbed my arm and squeezed my bicep with his strong hands and said, “Now listen, I understand how painful this failure is for you, but remember, this is nothing compared to how other people struggle in life!” “I understand, dad!” I said. “Now you get up right now and get back to work,” he said as he walked out of the room. That day I felt my father’s love and authority shake all my senses. The story of my grandfather gave me perspective. Now to answer your question, “Why do I feel like a failure? Question: Why are so many smart and diligent people successful in school but fail in real life?
Answer: Here’s “School-Smart” vs “Street-Smart” in a LEGO analogy: School is like getting a very complex LEGO set: The goal: “We expect you to put this Lego together,. We will show you how to do it! Follow the instructions and you will succeed!” So, we go from first grade through to sixth grade. In each grade, we get a set of instructions to follow: For example, this is first grade: Attention! If we fail to meet the required standards, we WON’T be able to move forward. If we DO meet the standards, we will be allowed to move to the next level — each level stacks upon the other, growing in complexity. If we complete elementary, we move on to middle school, and then to high school: Once we successfully finish high school, we move on to college. We continue “stacking” up ALL the sets of instructions, meeting the standards. If we don’t do it EXACTLY as expected, we will fail! Finally, the day comes … We celebrate … CONGRATULATIONS! We all get a “certificate” that proves we are capable of following very complex instructions. Then, we face the real world … The real world is also like Lego, but with NO INSTRUCTIONS! We feel confused and overwhelmed. “What should I do?” we ask ourselves. We urgently need someone to tell us what to do (boss). After all, we were all trained to FOLLOW instructions, indoctrinated, not really educated. What’s the difference? Indoctrination teaches us WHAT to think, not HOW to think! So, to answer your question, why are so many smart and diligent people successful in school but fail in real life? Being “school-smart” is radically different than being “street-smart.” Do you want to be “street-smart?” Consider this: We are now in an age where computers, algorithms and robots, are unbeatable at FOLLOWING instructions. If our value to the world is being good at following instructions, we then do NOT stand a chance at succeeding in today’s new economic environment. Who will win? “Street-Smart” in the new economy means we have extraordinary creative skills, meaning that we can innovate and think “outside the box.” Creativity CANNOT be automated! Computers, robots and algorithms CANNOT compete with us in creativity. Well, at least not yet … Schools MUST stop “standardizing” us. We are all different and that’s where success comes from, from our unique abilities and strengths that make us stand out in this competitive world. We now live in a very different world. Our educational system was built and perfected to serve the Industrial Age. The Industrial Age was all about competing with efficiencies. Following instructions with excellence increased productivity. Today that work belongs to machines, not to us. Today the world belongs to CREATORS! There are NO instructions ahead of us! The way we solved things yesterday is now outdated. Change is only accelerating. The sooner we understand this, the better chance we all have at succeeding in this world of exponential change. #BeBusinessSmart

Question: What would you do when you get stuck in business?
Answer: “Hey, Pete, I just purchased a new Land Cruiser. Let’s take it off-road to test!” My friend immediately agreed. We had no idea what lay ahead of us that day. Soon we found ourselves riding over boulders, pits, ditches and sandy areas. The powerful SUV conquered everything without a problem. That was until we encountered the river. “This is where the fun begins!” I told Pete as we approached the slow-moving waters. The four wheels were engaged with traction. The water slowly started to rise while we moved forward. As we approached the other side of the river, I felt one tire lose traction. I quickly turned the wheels to find solid ground. We kept moving. We were almost out of the water, when the mud got thicker. I felt the weight of the car sink into the mud. We stopped moving. “Are we stuck?” Peter asked. “No worries, Pete, I got this!” I said while turning the wheels and giving it more power. The mud splattered all around us. “This is the beauty of these machines, Pete. They will get out of anything!” Pete looked at me quietly. I smiled back, still fully confident that we we’re going to get out of this mud easily. I turned the wheels searching for traction. I went forward and used the reverse repeatedly, but the more I accelerated, the deeper we got stuck in the mud. “You should stop, Hector,” Peter said. I didn’t want to give up. “I can do this, Pete!” I said while pushing the gas pedal even harder. This obviously turned into a very frustrating and costly weekend. What was I thinking? Well, the truth was that I was not thinking! I had lost my mind trying to solve this problem following my instincts. I had used so much energy that now we couldn’t get out of this gigantic pile of mud! To answer your question, what would you do when you get stuck in business? It’s not uncommon for us entrepreneurs to spin our wheels. Sometimes indecision can take control of me, but for me, I can be really dangerous when my persistence kicks in and I find no progress. Result? I stop thinking. All this wasted energy starts to erode my patience. I know this is the perfect time to make significant changes, but I don’t have the mind for it; I have instincts. I may not notice it right away, but eventually frustration will start to control my mind. This is when I must stop as soon as possible, because when our business is not moving forward, it will eventually start to slide backwards. The Entrepreneurial Frustration As entrepreneurs, we’re driven. We’re self motivated and commonly fired up by passion — the very same ‘fuel’ that makes us unstoppable. We’re doers, we take action. We don’t ask for permission, we go, we chase, we pursue, we go after our goals. Then, every so often, we fall flat on our face. Roadblocks get in our way, or maybe mistakes we were not aware of. I’ve been in this situation so many times, just like my SUV, stuck in the mud. Anger makes me lose my mind, and my instincts tell me to solve everything with my strength, to use my abilities. Frustrations take over our emotions. Emotions and business never mix well together. Emotions will get us spinning out of control and won’t let us think! Remember, the best way to solve our problems in business (or in life) is very simple: ASK FOR HELP! We all face roadblocks. Don't try to do this alone! Leave your pride, your energy, your stubbornness and your passion behind. Find help. There’s always someone who knows the solution to your problem. Stop trying to solve everything yourself. Business success is found in teamwork. #BeBusinessSmart
